newsitem.title: INDIA: Flush of liquidity push down Indian call rates.
newsitem.headline: Flush of liquidity push down Indian call rates.

text.p: Indian call money rates opened at 2.25-3.0 percent on Thursday and was quoted at 2.00-2.25 percent in latest deals, bank dealers said.
Call rates closed at these levels on Wednesday.
Dealers said a surfeit of funds with the banking system had pushed down call rates to unusually low levels.
Many dealers said the cut in cash reserve ratio on October 26, which released over 20 billion rupees of locked up bank funds, could not explain the flush of liquidity.
One dealer said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s dollar purchases were adding to the pool of rupees in the system.
"There is also expectation of additional fund flow after banks start lending out of their FCNR funds," the dealer said, referring to expatriate Indian dollar account.
The RBI allowed banks to lend out of their FCNR accounts to local firms in its monetary policy announced on October 19.
Some dealers called the current call rates an "aberration."
